naslov: LeBron James: 'Too early to be talking Finals' after 76ers' blistering start
tekst:
DETROIT -- Fresh off another impressive win, Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James cautioned against any championship proclamations despite a blistering 8-1 start to the season and what that record usually means for a James-led team.
The previous four times James has started the season at least 7-1, his team has made the NBA Finals. 
"It's too early to be talking about the Finals and things of that nature on Nov. 4," James said after the Sixers beat the Detroit Pistons 112-106 on Wednesday night. "So we'll continue just to buy into what we want to do. ... We got a good team. Guys vibe with one another, guys like each other, guys enjoy being around each other."
The victory over Detroit avenged Philadelphia's only loss of the season. It was one of forward Jaylen Brown's best games as a Sixer, as he finished with a season-high 30 points and a game-saving block on Pistons point guard Cade Cunningham. Joel Embiid added 26 points and 15 rebounds for Philadelphia. ​
76ers coach Nick Nurse shared James' sentiment.
"I wouldn't read any super long-term stuff into anything, cause it's early," Nurse said. "I think we feel like that was another game where it feels like we're getting a touch better. ... But the goal right now is to stretch out those good periods of play and minimize those bad periods of play."
​It's the Sixers' first time starting 4-0 on the road since 2000-01, their last NBA Finals appearance. This is also the fifth time in the past 50 seasons that the 76ers have started 4-0 or better on the road. They made the NBA Finals in each of the previous four instances.
"Those teams just had consistency throughout the whole year, and every day we wanted to get better, every day," James said. "We didn't want to take too many steps backwards. Like I said, it can happen throughout the course of a marathon, but we understood what the assignment was and we all held each other accountable. And I think early on, I kind of see that here as well."
There was some injury concern for Sixers star Tyrese Maxey near the end of Wednesday's win. The point guard injured his right pinkie finger while attempting to split a double-team in the final seconds. In the locker room afterward, a Sixers athletic trainer briefly looked at Maxey's swollen finger.
"I'll be fine," Maxey said, adding after a reporter pointed out it looked swollen, "You wouldn't believe me if I told you this is how my finger's looked all season since last year. But I'm fine."
Center Adem Bona also exited the game in the fourth quarter with what Nurse said was a neck injury. Nurse said Bona appeared to be OK but that he would have an official update Thursday.
James finished with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. He will return to where he began his career when the Sixers play at the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday.
"We know we got a long way to go," James said.
